value: One of the main white grapes around San Patricio del Chañar, suited to the cool nights of northern Patagonia.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina Neuquén sheet (INV data): Chardonnay listed among main varieties of Añelo / San Patricio del Chañar | Wine Spectator: Patagonia's cool nights allow cooler climate wines such as Pinot Noir and Chardonnay to thrive (Patagonia wide, not Añelo specific)

value: One of the main red grapes around San Patricio del Chañar, a variety that does well in the windswept valleys of northern Patagonia.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina Neuquén sheet: Merlot among main varieties of San Patricio del Chañar | Wine Folly: Neuquén and Río Negro, wind swept regions where Pinot Noir and Merlot thrive

value: One of the main red grapes around San Patricio del Chañar, suited to the cool nights and constant wind of northern Patagonia.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina Neuquén sheet: Pinot Noir among main varieties; strong winds, cold nights | Wine Folly: Pinot Noir and Merlot thrive in wind swept Neuquén and Río Negro | Wine Spectator: cool nights let Pinot Noir and Chardonnay thrive in Patagonia

value: With Malbec, one of the main red grapes of the valley and of Salta's high vineyards.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina Salta sheet: Cabernet Sauvignon among main varieties of Cafayate GI | Wine Spectator: Salta key varieties Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Torrontés | Vinous (Joaquín Hidalgo, hosted by Wines of Argentina): Malbec and Cabernet built the region's reputation; Cabernet 'king of northern Argentine reds'

value: The valley's main red grape, now also planted in ever higher sites of the Calchaquí Valley.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina Salta sheet: Malbec first of Cafayate GI main varieties | Wine Spectator: Salta key varieties Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Torrontés | Vinous: move to higher elevations (Pucará, Angastaco, Molinos, Cachi); Malbec of the highest valleys

value: The signature white grape of the valley, a heritage variety of northern Argentina.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina Salta sheet: Torrontés Riojano among Cafayate GI main varieties | Wine Spectator: the north is home to the best examples of vibrant, floral Torrontés | Vinous: heritage varieties from Criolla Chica to Torrontés

value: Grown this high, it makes vivid, agile whites that rank among the most expressive examples of the grape.
source_notes: Wine Spectator: the north is home to the best examples of vibrant, floral Torrontés | Vinous: Cafayate a land of floral, agile Torrontés

value: One of the main red grapes of the Alto Valle, where it does well in the dry, windy Patagonian climate.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina Río Negro sheet: Merlot among main varieties of the Río Negro Upper Valley (General Roca department); wind a major climatic factor | Wine Folly: Pinot Noir and Merlot thrive in wind swept Neuquén and Río Negro

value: One of the main red grapes of the Alto Valle, suited to the cool nights and steady wind of northern Patagonia.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina Río Negro sheet: Pinot Noir among Upper Valley main varieties | Wine Folly: Pinot Noir thrives in Río Negro | Wine Spectator: cool nights let Pinot Noir thrive in Patagonia

value: Grown throughout the province alongside Malbec, from Luján de Cuyo and Maipú to the Uco Valley.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Cabernet Sauvignon in the Central Region (Luján de Cuyo, Maipú), Northern and Southern regions | Wine Spectator: Cabernet Sauvignon a key variety of Primera Zona and the Uco Valley

value: Grown in Luján de Cuyo and Maipú and in the higher Uco Valley, where it is one of the primary grapes.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Chardonnay in Luján de Cuyo and Maipú; a primary variety in the Uco Valley | Wine Spectator: Chardonnay a key variety of Primera Zona and the Uco Valley

value: The grape that made Mendoza's name, planted across the province, with Luján de Cuyo as its classic home.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Malbec put Mendoza on the world map; Luján de Cuyo the classic Malbec growing spot, 'Land of Malbec' | Wine Spectator: Malbec key variety in Primera Zona and Uco; Luján de Cuyo holds a large share of Mendoza's Malbec

value: One of the primary grapes of the valley's high vineyards, alongside Malbec.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Malbec, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Sémillon and Chardonnay are the primary varieties in the Uco Valley | Wine Spectator: Uco Valley key varieties include Malbec and Chardonnay

value: The main grape of the valley's high vineyards.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Malbec first of the Uco Valley's primary varieties | Wine Spectator: Malbec first of Uco Valley key varieties

value: Grown across the province, with the high Calingasta Valley singled out for it alongside Malbec.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina San Juan sheet: Cabernet Sauvignon among main varieties of Calingasta Valley GI | Wine Paths (travel company editorial): Calingasta has extraordinary potential for Malbec and Cabernet Sauvignon

value: One of the province's traditional red grapes, still widely planted.
source_notes: Wines of Argentina San Juan sheet (INV data): Bonarda among the larger red plantings of the province | Wine Paths (travel company editorial): traditional red varieties like Bonarda

value: With Sauvignon Blanc, one of the valley's two signature grapes, suited to its cool, foggy climate.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay the Casablanca Valley's most iconic varieties | The Wine Society: the cool climate is suitable for sauvignon blanc, chardonnay and pinot noir

value: Grown in the valley's cool, foggy sites, which are among the best known in Chile for the grape.
source_notes: The Wine Society: cool climate suitable for pinot noir | Wine Folly (Real Frontier): Casablanca makes outstanding Pinot Noir | Wine Folly (Best wines): best Pinot regions toward the coast, including Casablanca

value: With Chardonnay, one of the valley's two signature grapes, grown in vineyards cooled by fog and Pacific breezes.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay the most iconic varieties | The Wine Society: cool, foggy conditions shape the sauvignon blanc

value: So close to the cold Pacific, it gives tense wines with a mineral, faintly salty edge alongside the fruit.
source_notes: Wine & Spirits (R. DelRocco Terrazas, notes by Patricio Tapia): proximity to the coast gives natural acidity and a touch of saltiness; electric tension with mineral and citrus notes | Wines of Chile: vibrant whites with a distinctive minerality

value: One of the valley's main red grapes, alongside Carménère and Merlot.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: particular propensity for Carménère, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot | Wine Folly: Colchagua offers elegant, Bordeaux styled Cabernet

value: Colchagua Cabernet often leans to an elegant style, deep in colour and fresh enough to age well.
source_notes: Wine Folly: for a more elegant, Bordeaux styled Cabernet, Colchagua | Wines of Chile: Colchagua reds of excellent color, great freshness and very good cellaring capacity (said of the valley's reds in general)

value: The valley's best known grape, at its finest from old, unirrigated vines in Apalta.
source_notes: Wine Folly: 'The place for Carménère', look for Los Lingues or Apalta | The Wine Society: Apalta's standout unirrigated old vine carmenère | Wines of Chile: particular propensity for Carménère

value: Grown on the cool coastal slopes alongside Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: great potential for Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir on the coastal slopes | Wine Folly: San Antonio and Leyda among the sources of Chilean Chardonnay

value: With Sauvignon Blanc, the grape the Leyda zone is best known for, grown on cool slopes near the ocean.
source_notes: The Wine Society: Leyda became the region for sauvignon blanc and pinot noir | Wines of Chile: great potential for Pinot Noir | Wine Folly: Leyda, closest vineyards to the ocean, look for Pinot Noir and Syrah

value: The grape that made Leyda's name, grown on cool slopes close to the Pacific.
source_notes: The Wine Society: Leyda became the region for sauvignon blanc and pinot noir | Wines of Chile: great potential for Sauvignon Blanc near the coast

value: So near the ocean it makes light, taut wines with sharp acidity and a mineral edge.
source_notes: Wine & Spirits (Patricio Tapia notes): Leyda Sauvignon light and tight with a firm line of acidity; San Antonio example tart and succulent | Wines of Chile: San Antonio whites renowned for minerality and intense acidity

value: Grown alongside Pinot Noir as one of the valley's two reds, in a cool climate style.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Leyda, look for Pinot Noir and Syrah | Wines of Chile: inland, some of the most intense cool climate Syrahs in the country | The Wine Society: Matetic's San Antonio vineyards produce superb syrah

value: Grown in the cool coastal part of the valley rather than the warm interior.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir thriving in the coastal zone; reds traditional inland | Wine Folly: best Pinot regions tend to be toward the coast in Aconcagua

value: Favoured by the valley's cool conditions, it is the red the valley is best known for.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: conditions favourable for Burgundian varieties, Chardonnay and especially Pinot Noir | Wine Folly: Bío Bío, look for Pinot Noir

value: One of the white grapes suited to the valley's cool climate, alongside Sauvignon Blanc and Gewürztraminer.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: suitable for other white varieties such as Sauvignon Blanc and Riesling | The Wine Society: attractive gewürztraminer and riesling near Mulchén, riesling made dry or off dry

value: Long grown here for pisco, it is now also made into a rare dry white wine.
source_notes: Vinography (Alder Yarrow): the valleys' grapes long went to pisco; Mayu Pedro Ximénez tasted as a dry white | Wine Folly: dry P.X. is rare and found nowhere else in Chile except Elqui | Vintus (US importer of Mayu): these vines transitioned from pisco to wine

value: The main white grape of the valley, while Syrah leads the reds.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: leading strains of the region Syrah for reds and Sauvignon Blanc among the whites | Wine Folly: intriguing Sauvignon Blanc from Elqui (does not itself say main grape)

value: The valley's main red grape, grown both in fog cooled sites and high toward the Andes.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: Syrah the leading red | The Wine Society: Falernia's cool climate syrah; Alto Los Toros syrah blend in the Elqui Andes | Wine Folly: lean peppery Syrah from high altitude areas such as Elqui

value: From these cool, high sites it is leaner and more scented than the plump Syrah of Chile's warm central valleys.
source_notes: Wine Folly: lean, peppery style from high altitude areas such as Elqui, versus plump, smoky style of Maipo and Colchagua | The Wine Society: Falernia cool climate syrah scented with tar and violets (single producer)

value: With País, one of the valley's two traditional grapes, grown mostly on old bush vines.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: traditional varieties País and Moscatel de Alejandría predominate | Wine Folly: lots of old vine Cinsault, País and Muscat in Itata | Wine Anorak (Jamie Goode): most of Chile's Muscat is in Itata

value: With Moscatel de Alejandría, one of the valley's two traditional grapes, and a source of old vine reds.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: País and Moscatel de Alejandría predominate | Wine Folly: intriguing old vine País from Maule, Bío Bío and Itata | Wine Anorak: most País is in Maule and Itata

value: The valley's signature grape, grown near the coast where morning fog and limestone soils shape it.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: high end, fresh and mineral Chardonnay adapted to the coastal area | World of Fine Wine (Amanda Barnes): Chardonnay and Pinot Noir putting Limarí on the map | The Wine Society: chardonnays from limestone rich soils

value: Grown with Chardonnay in the cool coastal part of the valley, and one of the two grapes behind its reputation.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: Pinot Noir adapted very well to the coastal area | World of Fine Wine: Chardonnay and Pinot Noir putting Limarí on the map | The Wine Society: Maycas del Limarí pinots excellent

value: From cool limestone sites near the coast it is more delicate than most Chilean Pinot Noir, with a bracing, mineral freshness.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Limarí and Bío Bío Pinot more delicate and floral | World of Fine Wine: bracing, mineral character with finesse and persistence

value: Grown in the cool coastal part of the valley, alongside Chardonnay.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: Sauvignon Blanc adapted very well to the coastal area | World of Fine Wine: cool climate ideal for steely Sauvignon Blanc

value: Grown both in the cool coastal part of the valley and in warmer sites inland.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: Syrah adapted very well to the coastal area | The Wine Society: warmer inland sites suit viognier and syrah

value: The cool climate gives a sleeker, more vibrant Syrah than the plump style of Chile's warmer valleys.
source_notes: World of Fine Wine: svelte Syrah | Wine Folly (Real Frontier): vibrant, complex Syrah in this cool climate with limestone | Wine Folly (red guide): plump, smoky style in Maipo and Colchagua

value: The valley's main grape and the root of its fame, grown from the Andes foothills of Alto Maipo down to warmer, lower sites.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: main variety planted is Cabernet Sauvignon | Wine Folly: Chile's classic home of Cabernet Sauvignon, Macul and Puente Alto | The Wine Society: Upper Maipo cabernet firm and linear; warmer lower Maipo softer and fruitier

value: Grown alongside Cabernet Sauvignon, with the gravelly banks of the river around Isla de Maipo suited to it.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: Merlot, Syrah and Carménère thrive in the valley | The Wine Society: the gravelly banks of Isla de Maipo suit carmenère

value: One of the valley's main red grapes, alongside Merlot.
source_notes: Wines of Chile: Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot thrive | Wine Folly: in Maule look for Cabernet Franc, spicy herbaceous Cabernet Sauvignon and Carignan

value: From old, dry farmed bush vines it gives fresh, taut reds with lively acidity and firm structure.
source_notes: The Wine Society: old vine carignan has fresh acidity and good structure; unirrigated bush vines make fresh and taut wines | Wine Folly: Carignan in Itata and Maule lean and fresh with great acidic structure

value: A traditional grape of the valley, grown largely on old vines that now give País reds of note.
source_notes: Wine Folly: very intriguing old vine País from the Maule Valley, Bío Bío and Itata | Wine Anorak: most País is in Maule and Itata, now bottled to show terroir
